claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles can be prepared by liquid-phase laser ablation.
A nanoparticle fraction centered near 3 nm can be obtained for the proposed CoCrFeMnNi comparison.
Centrifugation-based size selection can produce a CoCrFeMnNi fraction centered near 10 nm from the synthesized distribution.
Premelting and melting behavior in equimolar CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles is governed primarily by nanoparticle size through the surface-to-volume ratio.
Smaller nanoparticles have a higher surface-to-volume ratio than larger nanoparticles of the same geometry.
A higher surface-to-volume ratio increases the fraction of under-coordinated surface atoms.
Under-coordinated surface atoms contribute less cohesive energy than fully coordinated interior atoms.
The increased fraction of under-coordinated atoms in smaller particles lowers the particle's effective cohesive energy.
Lower effective cohesive energy reduces the temperature at which premelting begins.
Lower effective cohesive energy broadens the temperature interval over which melting occurs.
Approximately 3 nm CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will show premelting at a lower temperature than approximately 10 nm particles of the same composition.
Approximately 3 nm CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will have a broader melting transition than approximately 10 nm particles.
Approximately 10 nm CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles will have a sharper and higher-temperature melting onset than approximately 3 nm particles.
The approximately 10 nm particles have higher cohesive energy per particle than the approximately 3 nm particles.
Size effects should dominate premelting and melting behavior over the approximately 3–10 nm diameter range when composition is held constant.
Subtle compositional inhomogeneities may influence nanoparticle melting behavior independently of size.
Local atomic ordering may influence nanoparticle melting behavior independently of size.
Failure to observe both a statistically significant lower premelting onset and a broader melting interval in the smaller fraction would falsify the proposed size-governed hypothesis.
